text:
incidents-bot: ALERT 1719876543 — hosted.api.v1.generate.p99 > 2000ms for 4m (us-west1). severity=P2. streaming stalls observed. runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/latency-p99

sara (oncall): I'm paged, taking this. starting triage.

mike_r: on call infra, joining. ping me if you need node-level access.

sara (oncall): quick summary from console: p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 2.2s, error rate steady. streaming stall metric (streaming.chunks_stalled) spike correlates w/ p99. Affected tenant set: multiple heavy streaming customers in us-west1 (approx 8%-12% of traffic).

lee_ops: I see GPU errors on gpu-node-07 and gpu-node-08 in the last 10m. NVML ECC corrected count rising, and kernel shows thermal warnings.

anita: can we failover traffic to other us-west1 capacity or degrade to non-streaming fallback? We should surface to customers asap.

sara (oncall): yes. plan: 1) isolate offending nodes, 2) route new streaming requests away from pool-gpu-1, 3) enable fallback non-streaming route for streaming clients for affected customers, 4) if needed, increase capacity from reserved pool. executing now.

mike_r: running quick checks — connecting to node.

lee_ops: attaching kernel tail:```
[ 2024-06-02T14:07:12.123Z] EDAC MC0: CE error: GPU 0: device ecc corrected error count increased to 34
[ 2024-06-02T14:07:12.124Z] nvidia: GPU 0000:05:00.0: Corrected ECC error
[ 2024-06-02T14:08:01.456Z] thermal: int3400 thermal sensor: critical temp 101C, GPU throttling engaged
[ 2024-06-02T14:08:03.789Z] nv_peer_mem: Warning: PCIe link issues on bus 0000:05:00.0
```

sara (oncall): thanks. that lines up with streaming stalls — KV cache building + stalls when device pauses.

mike_r: draining gpu-node-07 from pool-gpu-1. command: `kubectl patch node gpu-node-07 -p '{"spec": {"unschedulable": true}}'` and `redwood infra node drain gpu-node-07 --force --timeout 10m`

infra-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2024-4321 and PagerDuty incident PD-654321.

anita: I've pushed a per-tenant emergency route override: streaming -> fallback-stream (non-streaming chunked responses) for affected tenant group. This will cause higher latency for long responses but prevents stalls. Activated at 14:12 UTC.

sara (oncall): running correlation: GPU ECC spikes started ~14:05 UTC, p99 spike ~14:06 UTC, streaming stalls reported by clients starting ~14:08 UTC. Looks like hardware degradation triggered runtime stalls.

lee_ops: NVML shows sustained GPU temp 100-104C and power capping engaged. Suspect thermal throttling on SAMSUNG A100-80GB node (hot aisle issue).

mike_r: manual node reboot initiated (gpu-node-07). Will monitor ECC counts after reboot. If ECC corrected continues to increase, we'll out-of-band isolate and replace hardware via provider ticket.

sara (oncall): mitigation checklist updated: drain, reboot, replace if ECC persists, route overrides active, scale up warm pool by +20% in us-west1.

anita: scaling warm GPU pool: `redwood scale pool-gpu-1 --delta 4 --region us-west1` — started. ETA for new nodes 6-8 minutes.

infra-bot: Autoscaler triggered additional dedicated capacity in us-west1 (3 nodes) to maintain throughput.

mike_r: Reboot complete on gpu-node-07. Post-reboot NVML: ECC corrected count reset to 0 but within 5m jumped back to 5 -> indicates failing DIMM or persistent electrical issue. Logged hardware ticket with provider and flagged for replacement.

lee_ops: telemetry shows p99 improving to ~950ms after draining and fallback rules. streaming stalls metric down ~85% from peak.

sara (oncall): customer impact estimate: 9% of overall requests in us-west1 experienced >SLO latency; error rate not increased; no data loss. Affected customers notified via status page draft (prepared).

anita: posted interim status to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating higher tail latency impacting streaming in US-WEST. Mitigations in place: routing overrides and capacity increases.", and PM copy to customer success queued.

mike_r: provider responded to hardware ticket — scheduled replace for gpu-node-07 next maintenance window ~2h. We'll continue to route traffic away and keep node cordoned.

sara (oncall): handoff — I'm going offline in 15m. mike_r, can you take warm-oncall until node replacement completes? I will update incident doc and attach logs.

mike_r: taking over. I'll keep monitoring p99 and streaming stalls and coordinate hardware replacement. Add me to the incident ticket.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2024-4321 updated: status=mitigated, severity=P2, active=false (mitigations applied).

sara (oncall): final notes before handoff: root cause appears to be a degrading GPU (rising ECC corrected errors + thermal throttling) causing device-level stalls and backpressure in the serving runtime. Immediate mitigations: cordon/drain node(s), route streaming -> fallback, hot-scale pool. Follow-ups: replace affected GPU, run a thermal survey of us-west1 rack cooling, add automatic ECC threshold alert and auto-drain rule in runbook, update postmortem with RCA.

mike_r: acknowledged. I'll file follow-up tasks: HW-2024-77 (replace GPU), OPS-2024-201 (thermal audit), RNR-2024-12 (runbook update).

anita: notify support & top 10 affected customers with mitigation summary and ETA for full restoration.

sara (oncall): thanks team. handing off. :wave: 

mike_r: logging last check at 15:10 UTC: p99 ~ 620ms, streaming stalls near baseline. Closing active mitigation loop — monitoring.

incidents-bot: NOTE — keep thread open until replacement confirmed. Add final postmortem link when available.
